ai.title: Fix request file error
ai.summary: Corrects `requestFile` to return `null` on missing keys. Tightens `requestFiles` logic to match `requestId` exclusively, removing unsafe path array comparison. Updates `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to strip debug `console.log`.

eli5.text: When you open a file that doesn't exist, the assistant now tells you clearly it's not there instead of getting stuck or showing a confusing error. The assistant also checks requests more carefully: it matches each file request to a unique ID, rather than comparing lists of paths, which avoids grabbing the wrong files when multiple requests happen at once. You may also notice the assistant no longer logs every step while working, since those extra debug notes were removed.

ai.title: Trim messages to fit 200k token limit
ai.summary: Added trimMessagesToFitTokenLimit in backend/src/util/messages.ts to truncate conversation history when exceeding the 200k token cap. mainPrompt now calculates system prompt tokens and passes trimmed messages to promptClaudeStream, preserving the last user message and recent context while dropping older turns. Includes new evals/test-repos/manifold submodule.

eli5.text: Long conversations can now be trimmed automatically before reaching the assistant. When you have a back-and-forth that exceeds the maximum conversation size, the system now removes the oldest parts of the chat while always keeping your most recent message, so you lose the distant history but preserve the current thread. This keeps single chats from being cut off mid-sentence when they run too long, and it applies specifically after the conversation hits that size cap.

ai.title: Update README local dev setup instructions
ai.summary: README.md local dev setup now documents separate `bun run start-server`, `start-web`, and `start-client` commands instead of the `start-dev.sh` script. Build steps use explicit `cd` sequences to ensure correct package directory resolution. The `start-web` step notes Docker dependency for account authorization.

eli5.text: The written guide for getting the software running on your own computer has been rewritten. Instead of a single helper that launched everything together, you now run three separate commands in three separate windows: one to start the main application, one to start a required support service (which needs Docker installed), and one to start the part you interact with. The setup steps also changed slightly so they correctly find each piece of the software regardless of where you are in the file system. If you follow the guide today, you will notice it walks you through opening multiple terminal windows and typing these individual commands rather than using the one combined command from before.

ai.title: CLI adds bang prefix for terminal commands
ai.summary: CLI accepts `!` prefix to run terminal commands. `npm-app/src/cli.ts` strips `!` before `handleRunTerminalCommand` and prints stdout when `!` commands fail. `npm-app/src/menu.ts` help now documents `!command` instead of `/run <command>`.

eli5.text: When you type a command that starts with an exclamation point in the CLI, it now runs that command in your terminal. Previously, you had to type a longer prefix like '/run ' before your command; now you can just type '!command' instead. If your command fails, the program also shows you more detail about what went wrong. You would notice this because the help menu shows the new shortcut instead of the old one.

ai.title: terminal.ts add quoted not found case
ai.summary: terminal.ts `isNotACommand` adds check for `' not found` alongside existing `command not found` and `: not found`. Linux shells quote failed commands, causing detection miss. Scope: `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts`. New substring check covers single-quoted command names.

eli5.text: The error checker that looks for "command not found" messages now recognizes a third spelling that Linux shells use when they wrap the failed command in quotes. If you run a bad command in a Linux terminal, the assistant may have missed catching it before; now it should detect that case too. The change was made today in the internal toolset and is already live.
